skill.name: set-up-shopware-google-ads-enhanced-conversions
skill.description: Set up or troubleshoot Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for a Shopware 6 sales channel through Product Metrics. Check consent settings, Google customer data terms, and test order sync.
skill.summary: Configure and check Enhanced Conversions for Shopware 6 and Google Ads through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, documentation links, or routine setup rather than malicious execution or reconnaissance. Real risks include an unpinned installer, a general-purpose remote connector, and order queries that exceed the verification task. The review also found gaps in authorization, credential handling, and consent verification, but no evidence of deliberate exfiltration or an attempt to manipulate the audit.

remediation.issue: The installer runs an unpinned package and retrieves an unpinned skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and verify both the installer version and the skill revision. Require explicit approval before running any installer.

remediation.issue: The remote connector and fallback workflow lack task-specific limits for account access and writes.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the workspace, storefront, and Google Ads client account with the merchant. Allowlist Google Ads setup operations and require approval before linking accounts, changing settings, or enabling data flows.

remediation.issue: Test-order verification can retrieve unnecessary commercial or customer-linked order data.
remediation.suggestion: Check a known synthetic order through a status-only lookup scoped to the verified storefront. Report sync status without order contents, margins, or customer classification.

remediation.issue: The skill permits credentials for unrelated integrations to pass through agent commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unrelated credential exceptions. Keep credentials in the vendor's authenticated browser or secure secret-entry flow and out of agent messages and command arguments.

remediation.issue: The verification steps do not show that outgoing fields respect consent choices.
remediation.suggestion: Use synthetic orders to test granted, denied, and withdrawn consent. Verify field presence or absence through redacted delivery diagnostics before reporting that consent is enforced.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials for Unrelated Integrations
semantic_findings.description: The secrets rule allows credentials for Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI to pass directly to a command. These credentials are unnecessary for Shopware and Google Ads and could enter tool traces or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exceptions are explicit, while Google Ads authorization is a browser step. No evidence shows that the command transport protects secrets or that any credentials were exposed.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Scope Can Expand Beyond Google Ads
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can proceed into prerequisite setup and agent writes without a general approval step. Its Shopware fallback also lists connecting Meta and ChatGPT Ads, outside the stated Google Ads task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow points to broader setup material and specifies protections for retries, deletes, and primary actions. It does not require separate approval for every new destination or other write.

semantic_findings.title: Consent Enforcement Is Not Verified
semantic_findings.description: The guide checks readiness and test order arrival but does not compare outgoing fields across consent choices. This can miss an incorrect consent mapping for hashed identifiers, country, or postcode.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The verification steps check application status, the banner, and order sync. They do not specify a denied-consent delivery check, and there is no evidence that the implementation bypasses consent.

content.user_title: Set Up Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Shopware
content.value_statement: Google Ads can miss Shopware purchases when browser identifiers are unavailable. Use Product Metrics to check server-side tracking, configure consent, and verify that a test order syncs.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP and identify completed steps.
Guide the merchant through pairing a Shopware sales channel and checking its Google Ads connection.
Identify the consent setting that corresponds to the banner on the storefront.
Guide a Google Ads administrator through customer data terms and interpret the Product Metrics readiness status.
Guide a paid test order in payment test mode and check whether it appears in Product Metrics.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a supported Shopware 6.7 installation, and a connected Google Ads client account with Merchant Center.
The merchant completes Shopware admin steps, Google approvals, and any changes to primary conversion actions.
A synced test order does not prove Google Ads matched the purchase to an ad click or received the expected consented fields.
Customer Match and bidding changes are outside this workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare a storefront for Enhanced Conversions
use_cases.description: Check whether your Shopware channel, Product Metrics workspace, and Google Ads account meet the setup requirements.

use_cases.title: Resolve a Google Ads readiness warning
use_cases.description: Use the readiness status to identify whether customer data terms, Data Manager acceptance, or the account connection needs attention.

use_cases.title: Validate an integration handoff
use_cases.description: Confirm the paired channel and banner, then document whether a synthetic test order synced without exposing customer information.

prompt_templates.title: List setup requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan the rollout before connecting any tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the prerequisites for Shopware 6 and Google Ads Enhanced Conversions through Product Metrics. Separate my browser steps from the status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Check current setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a workspace with an existing connection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my workspace and storefront scope before running read-only setup checks. Tell me which prerequisites are complete and what I should do next.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an account warning
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Product Metrics shows Action required.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me distinguish unaccepted Google customer data terms from a Data Manager rejection. Show the browser steps for my verified Google Ads account without changing settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a scoped test order
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: verify order sync after setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a synthetic paid order in payment test mode. Check only the known test order in my paired channel and report what sync alone cannot verify.

output_examples.input: Product Metrics says customer data terms are managed on another account. What should I do?
output: Confirm that the account number shown belongs to your Google Ads manager account.
Review and accept the customer data terms in that account. Then select Re-check in Product Metrics.

output_examples.input: My test order appears in Product Metrics. Does that mean Enhanced Conversions is working?
output: The order appearing in Product Metrics confirms that it synced from the paired Shopware channel.
It does not confirm which customer fields Google received or whether Google matched the purchase to an ad click.

best_practices: Confirm the Product Metrics workspace, Shopware sales channel, and Google Ads client account before approving any changes.
Match the consent setting to the banner shoppers actually see. Use synthetic orders to verify granted and denied consent when diagnostics are available.
Keep conversion actions secondary during testing. Leave pairing tokens and Google approvals in the appropriate browser interface.
anti_patterns: Do not paste pairing tokens, API credentials, or customer details into chat.
Do not list live customer orders when checking a known synthetic test order.
Do not treat a Ready status or an imported order as proof of consent enforcement or successful attribution.

faq.question: Is there a separate Enhanced Conversions switch in Product Metrics?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics adds eligible customer fields when server-side tracking is active. Google Ads may still require terms acceptance or an account setting.

faq.question: Do I need Google Tag Manager for this workflow?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics sends conversions through Google's Data Manager without requiring a Google tag change.

faq.question: Which fields are hashed?
faq.answer: Product Metrics hashes email, phone, and names with SHA-256. Billing country and postcode are not hashed when sent with the complete name and location fields.

faq.question: Can I use the built-in Shopware cookie manager?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave Configure consent set to Not configured in Product Metrics. Shopware then uses the Product Metrics advertising attribution choice.

faq.question: What happens when a visitor declines ad user data?
faq.answer: If the visitor allows ad storage, the purchase can still be sent without enhanced customer data. If neither permission is granted, the purchase is not sent.

faq.question: Who accepts Google's customer data terms?
faq.answer: A Google Ads administrator accepts the terms in the relevant account. If Product Metrics identifies a managing account, accept the terms there.
